purpose: This ingredient is the active part in many strong antiperspirant products that help control heavy sweating. It is used on the underarms to reduce sweat and help keep you feeling dry and comfortable throughout the day. It is often found in clinical-strength or prescription-strength antiperspirant products.
how_it_works: When you apply it to your skin, this ingredient temporarily plugs the sweat glands in your underarms so less sweat can reach the surface of your skin. Think of it like a tiny temporary stopper that blocks the sweat ducts. This does not affect how your body regulates its temperature overall, since sweat glands across the rest of your body still work normally.
common_side_effects: Some people may notice mild skin irritation, redness, itching, or a slight rash in the underarm area, especially if applied right after shaving. These reactions are usually mild and go away on their own.
warnings: Do not use on broken, irritated, or freshly shaved skin as this can cause stinging or irritation. Avoid getting it in your eyes. Do not use it on children under 12 years old without talking to a doctor first. If you develop a rash or severe irritation, stop using it and speak with your pharmacist or doctor.
typical_dosing: Apply a thin, even layer to clean dry underarms once daily, usually at night before bed for best results. Allow it to dry completely before dressing. You do not need to reapply every day once you notice good control of sweating.
